---
title: "Shared secret write"
description: "Dispatch-only workflows that generate one secret value and write it to every consumer without a human, a file or a log ever holding it."
updatedAt: "2026-11-21"
audience: developers
---

Some secrets are held by more than one Cloudflare Worker: the apps/web Workers
sign, and peer Workers verify. Every side must hold the same value, and
no person, file or log should ever see it. Two workflows generate or create the
value inside one job step, hand it to every destination over stdin, and read the
result back by name and type.

| Workflow | Writes | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `shared-secret-write.yaml` | One of the listed secrets to every Worker that issues or verifies it | `shared-secret-staging`, `shared-secret-production` |
| `shared-secret-copy.yaml` | The current value of a secret, from its GitHub secret, to the apps/web Workers only | `colab-production` or `meet-cloudflare-production` |
| `supabase-family-key.yaml` | A new `cf-web-families` Supabase secret key to `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` on opted-in web route family Workers | `supabase-family-key` |

## Shared secret write

Inputs are two choices: `secret` and `environment`. There is no free-text input.

| `secret` | Worker bindings |
| --- | --- |
| `ABUSE_GUARD_SECRET` | `ABUSE_GUARD_SECRETS` on `tuturuuu-abuse-guard`; `ABUSE_GUARD_SECRET` on the vinext Workers |
| `WEB_MULTI_ACCOUNT_SESSION_SECRET` | The same name on each web family Worker with auth and each vinext Worker |
| `ABUSE_GUARD_KEY_PEPPER` (production) | The same name on `tuturuuu-cms`, `tuturuuu-nova`, `tuturuuu-rewise` and the vinext Workers |
| `CLOUDFLARE_COORDINATION_TOKEN` (production) | `COORDINATION_TOKEN` on `tuturuuu-coordination`; `CLOUDFLARE_COORDINATION_TOKEN` on the other senders `tuturuuu-infrastructure` (the admin app's deployed Worker) and `tuturuuu-calendar`, and on the vinext Workers |
| `MASTERMIND_STORE_TOKEN` (production) | `MASTERMIND_STORE_TOKENS` on `tuturuuu-mastermind-store`; the web name on the vinext Workers |

The vinext Workers are `tuturuuu-web-vinext-<id>` for each family that
`apps/web/cloudflare/vinext/families.json` marks `activated`. A family is
activated once its Worker is published and routed by the gateway, because
preflight refuses to write while any listed Worker is missing.

Print the destinations, dual-accept facts, no-outage order and user impact for
a secret before dispatching. The command needs no credentials and sends no
request:

```bash
node scripts/ci/shared-secret.mjs plan <secret> <environment> [all|web]
```

Cloudflare serves tuturuuu.com, and rollback means a previous Cloudflare
version. Every destination is a Worker secret; nothing is written to Vercel.

Worker names for `staging` carry a `-staging` suffix.
The web family Workers are the `worker` entries of
`apps/web/cloudflare/opennext/families.json` at the checked-out commit (skipping
`enabled: false`, and `auth: false` for this secret). While that file does not
exist the list is `tuturuuu-web-api-identity`.

The job refuses to run unless it is dispatched on `main` from a commit that
descends from `018eecf2` (the abuse-guard `ratelimit` family). In order, one
step:

1. `preflight`: every target Worker exists and the Cloudflare credential is
   present. Nothing is written if a Worker is missing. Preflight does not
   compare versions: a secret write deploys each Worker's latest uploaded
   version, so before dispatching, confirm that every target's latest upload
   is the version it serves (`cf workers versions list` against
   `cf workers deployments list`). A Worker with a newer undeployed upload
   would ship that upload with the secret.
2. Generates the value with `openssl rand -base64 48`, masks it with
   `::add-mask::`, and keeps it in one shell variable.
3. Pipes it on stdin to every Worker write, in the order the plan lists them.
4. Unsets the variable.
5. `verify`: each Worker has exactly one `secret_text` binding of that name. Output is
   names and types only; any mismatch fails the job.

Re-running the job rotates the value everywhere. For `ABUSE_GUARD_SECRET` that
means the Worker accepts only the new value as soon as the Worker write lands,
and every web Worker takes the new value in the same job.

The writes use the Cloudflare REST API from
`scripts/ci/shared-secret-api.mjs`, with the value only in a request body. No
command line, URL, header, environment file, step output, artifact or cache holds
it, and error messages carry the HTTP status and numeric provider codes only.

Credentials, by name, from the protected environment: `COLAB_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`
(a Cloudflare token that can edit the Workers in account
`e8912e2867beecc673d171907bf09649`).

## Copying a current value

A secret whose current value is readable somewhere (a GitHub secret its owning
deploy publishes, or an operator host) is copied to the web Workers without a
rotation. Scope `web` writes only the vinext Workers and never the peer or
sender Workers, which already hold the same value.

`shared-secret-copy.yaml` does this for the GitHub-held values, with one job per
source environment:

| `secret` | Source | Job (environment) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CRON_CONTROL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` | Repository secret of the same name | `copy-repo-secret` (`colab-production`) |
| `TUTURUUU_DEVBOX_CONTROL_TOKEN` | Repository secret `DEVBOX_CONTROL_INTERNAL_TOKEN` | `copy-repo-secret` (`colab-production`) |
| `MEET_REALTIME_TOKEN_SECRET` | Environment secret of the same name | `copy-meet` (`meet-cloudflare-production`) |

Dispatch it on the `production` branch after a production sync, so the copied
tooling is the synced main commit. Each job runs only on that ref (job condition
and a `test "$GITHUB_REF" = refs/heads/production` step), which both job
environments already admit, and writes with
`WEB_OPENNEXT_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (Workers Scripts edit), resolves exactly one
source, unsets it after moving it into one masked shell variable, pipes it to
`write workers <secret> production web` and verifies names and types.

Operator-held values (`MASTERMIND_FLEET_PUBLISHER_SECRET` on the publisher host,
`MASTERMIND_PUSH_HMAC_SECRET` in the push hub, the Keychain copy of
`MASTERMIND_STORE_TOKEN`) are copied from a shell on the host that holds them,
with `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` set:

```bash
node scripts/ci/shared-secret.mjs write workers <secret> production web < <0600-file>
```

Scope `all` is refused for a secret that is not minted. `write` accepts only
`workers`.

## Vercel environment sync

`scripts/ci/web-cf-env-sync.mjs` copies the production environment of the web
project (project and team-shared variables) onto one apps/web Worker:

```bash
node scripts/ci/web-cf-env-sync.mjs --worker <name> \
  --names apps/web/cloudflare/opennext/<family>.env.json [--names ...] \
  [--apply] [--vars-out <0600-file>] [--report <file>] [--deny <NAME>]
```

A name list is a family inventory (its four synced sections, minus `unset`
names) or a plain list; `*` selects every key. Without `--apply` nothing is
revealed or written. With `--apply` each value is revealed one at a time and all
reveals finish before any write: `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` names become plain-text vars,
the rest secrets in one version. Output carries names, Vercel types and
destinations only. Statuses:

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `write` | Readable in Vercel and free on the Worker |
| `missing` | `sensitive` in Vercel, which cannot be revealed; supply it with the workflows above |
| `absent` | Not set in Vercel production (the code default applies) |
| `kept` | Not in Vercel, already a plain-text var from the deploy config |
| `skip` / `conflict` | Listed as `unset`, a Vercel system value, or bound on the Worker with another type |

`DENIED_NAMES` holds names that are never copied or reported
(`DEEPGRAM_API_KEY`, a removed integration).

With `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` set the script uses the Cloudflare API and sets vars
through the script settings endpoint, keeping every other binding as `inherit`.
Without it, it uses the `cf` CLI login: bindings come from the latest version,
secrets go through `cf workers secrets bulk-edit` with a mode `0600` file that
is deleted afterwards, and vars go to `--vars-out` for the deploy config,
because the CLI has no settings write. Vars set on a Worker are replaced by its
next deploy unless the deploy config declares them; secrets persist.

The script only reads the Vercel archive. Vercel answers a reveal with
`403 challenge_required` when the token's
session needs a fresh sign-in. The script stops before writing anything; sign in
again with `vercel login` (or use a newly issued `VERCEL_TOKEN`) and rerun.

## Supabase family key

`supabase-family-key.yaml` takes `action: create` or `action: revoke`.
For `create` it
runs `preflight` (every selected Worker exists, and no key named
`cf-web-families` exists), creates the key (`type: secret`) in the production Supabase project, masks
the returned value, pipes it to `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` on each selected Worker, and
reads back the key name, id and type plus each Worker secret name and type. A
second run stops at `preflight`; it never creates a second key. If a Worker write
fails after key creation, use `revoke` before attempting `create` again.

Under the same protected job, `revoke` resolves the unique secret key by its
exact mint name, `cf-web-families`, deletes it by ID and confirms it is absent.
A missing key is already revoked. Revocation invalidates the key on every
recipient immediately. Worker binding names remain in place until they are
overwritten by a subsequent create. Both actions require the environment's
dedicated credential to be present. The revoke branch unsets it before calling
Supabase and can run when family configs are missing.

A family is selected only if `supabaseSecret: true` is set in
`apps/web/cloudflare/opennext/families.json`. Routing's `enabled` flag is
independent. Each opted-in family config must declare its exact Worker name,
the reviewed Cloudflare account and `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` as required.
All family Worker configs set `APP_COORDINATION_TOKEN_DISABLE_SUPABASE_FALLBACK=1`
so a database key cannot sign or verify app coordination tokens. Required
coordination secrets must be provisioned independently before activation.
A missing or mismatched config blocks key creation for the entire set.
The `public-docs` family stays outside this key's recipient set.

Provision the `supabase-family-key` GitHub environment with required reviewers,
admin bypass disabled and a single custom deployment policy for the branch
`main`. Place `SUPABASE_FAMILY_KEY_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` in that environment
with Workers Scripts:Edit only for account `e8912e2867beecc673d171907bf09649`.
The workflow uses the existing repository secret `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`.
Both credentials stay in the operator step, with shell tracing disabled and
masking configured before the provider scripts run.

## Operator token

The abuse-guard operator token (`ABUSE_GUARD_OPERATOR_TOKEN`, used for
`/control/stop`, `/control/resume` and `/control/state`) is not written by these
workflows. Whoever needs a copy regenerates it through the Cloudflare deploy path
and keeps it in a mode `0600` file.

## Regression coverage

`scripts/ci/shared-secret-copy.test.mjs` pins the copy workflow contract.
`scripts/ci/shared-secret-rotation.test.mjs` covers the activated vinext Workers, the
`web` scope (no peer or sender request), every coordination sender in one
mint, the mint-only `all` scope and the
offline `plan`. `scripts/ci/web-cf-env-sync.test.mjs` covers name-list
expansion, the plan statuses, the deny list, reveal-before-write, the 0600
temporary file and that no value reaches a URL, argv, log line or error.

`scripts/ci/shared-secret-write.test.mjs` pins the workflow contract (dispatch
only, choice inputs, `main` guard, the commit floor, protected environments,
read-only token, existing full-SHA action pins, credentials by name, mask before
first use, the value only on stdin, no `--value`, no `echo`, no Wrangler) and
exercises the scripts with a provider double: the value appears only in write
bodies, never in URLs, headers, output or error text, and every readback fails
closed on a missing, duplicate or wrongly typed entry.
